name: Ashmarihar Kashayam

sections.introduction: Ashmarihar Kashayam is a classical Ayurvedic herbal decoction traditionally used for the management of Ashmari (urinary calculi or stones), Sharkara (gravel), Sikata (sand-like urinary deposits), and painful urinary disorders associated with the kidneys and urinary bladder. The formulation contains several diuretic, anti-inflammatory, stone-breaking, and urinary tract soothing herbs that help support healthy urinary flow and reduce discomfort caused by urinary obstruction. The term “Ashmarihar” literally means “destroyer of stones.” In Ayurveda, Ashmari is considered a serious disorder caused by the vitiation of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha along with the accumulation of mineral deposits in the urinary system. This Kashayam is designed to dissolve or disintegrate urinary concretions, relieve spasms, improve urine flow, and reduce inflammation of the urinary tract.
sections.ingredients:
The following ingredients are used in the preparation of Ashmarihar Kashayam: 

 Pashanbheda (Bergenia ligulata) – Stone Breaker Herb 
 Sagwan Fruit (Tectona grandis) – Teak Fruit 
 Papita Root / Erand Karkati (Carica papaya) – Papaya Root 
 Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus) – Wild Asparagus 
 Gokshura / Gokhru (Tribulus terrestris) – Small Caltrops 
 Varuna Bark (Crataeva nurvala) – Three-Leaved Caper Bark 
 Kusha Root (Desmostachya bipinnata) – Sacred Grass Root 
 Kasa Root (Saccharum spontaneum) – Wild Sugarcane Root 
 Rice Plant Root (Oryza sativa) – Paddy Root 
 Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa) – Spreading Hogweed 
 Guduchi / Giloy (Tinospora cordifolia) – Heart-Leaved Moonseed 
 Chichda Root (traditionally identified regionally; often associated with urinary herbs) 
 Kheera Kakdi Seeds (Cucumis sativus) – Cucumber Seeds 
 Jatamansi (Nardostachys jatamansi) – Spikenard 
 Khurasani Ajwain Seeds (Hyoscyamus niger) – Henbane Seeds 


 Quantities 
 According to the classical formulation: 

 The first thirteen herbs are taken in equal quantities of 1 tola each (approximately 11–12 g each). 
 Jatamansi (Nardostachys jatamansi) and Khurasani Ajwain (Hyoscyamus niger) are taken in quantities of 2 tola each (approximately 23–24 g each). 

 The herbs are coarsely powdered (Jaukut Churna) for preparing the decoction. 

 Method of Preparation 
 All ingredients are cleaned properly and coarsely powdered. Approximately 1 tola (about 12 g) of the prepared herbal mixture is taken for each dose. The coarse powder is mixed with 16 tola water (approximately 180–190 ml water). The mixture is then boiled slowly until one-fourth quantity remains, which is approximately 45–50 ml. 
 The decoction is filtered while warm. 
 To this filtered Kashayam, one of the following may traditionally be added: 

 Shilajit – 5 ratti (approximately 600 mg) 
 Kshar Parpati – 10 ratti (approximately 1.2 g) 
 Jawakhar – 10 ratti (approximately 1.2 g) 

 The medicine is then administered warm.

Water for decoction: Approximately 16 tola (180–190 ml) 
 Final decoction quantity: One-fourth remaining (45–50 ml) 
 Frequency: Two to three times daily, depending on severity 

 In severe pain or urinary obstruction, the formulation may traditionally be administered every 2 hours under medical supervision.
sections.ayurvedic_properties:
Ashmarihar Kashayam possesses the following important Ayurvedic actions: 

 Mutrala – Diuretic 
 Ashmaribhedana – Stone-breaking 
 Shoolahara – Pain relieving 
 Shothahara – Anti-inflammatory 
 Vatanulomana – Regulates Vata 
 Mutravirechana – Promotes healthy urination 

 The formulation is designed to reduce urinary obstruction while soothing irritation and inflammation in the urinary tract.
sections.therapeutic_uses:
1. Ashmari (Urinary Stones) 
 The primary indication of this Kashayam is urinary calculi affecting the kidneys, ureters, or bladder. It helps by supporting gradual disintegration of stones, reducing burning and painful urination, promoting urinary flow and reducing spasmodic pain. Pashanbheda (Bergenia ligulata) and Varuna (Crataeva nurvala) are especially valued in Ayurveda for urinary stone disorders. 

 2. Sharkara and Sikata) 
 The formulation is also useful in gravel in urine, sand-like urinary deposits, small crystal formations and recurrent urinary sediment. These conditions are considered early stages of stone formation in Ayurveda. 

 3. Renal Colic and Bladder Pain 
 The decoction is traditionally administered in Vrikka Shool (kidney pain), Mutrashaya Shool (bladder pain) and painful urinary obstruction. Its antispasmodic and diuretic herbs help relieve discomfort and ease urine passage. 

 4. Urinary Inflammation 
 Several ingredients in the formulation soothe urinary irritation and inflammation. Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus) and Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa) provide cooling and anti-inflammatory effects. 

 Importance of Major Ingredients 
 Pashanbheda (Bergenia ligulata) 
 Traditionally famous as a stone-breaking herb, it is widely used in Ayurveda for: 

 Kidney stones 
 Burning urination 
 Urinary obstruction 
 Bladder irritation 


 Varuna (Crataeva nurvala) 
 Varuna bark is regarded as one of the best Ayurvedic herbs for urinary disorders. It supports: 

 Bladder health 
 Stone management 
 Healthy urine flow 
 Reduction of urinary swelling 


 Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa) 
 Purified Guggul is known for: 

 Anti-inflammatory action 
 Scraping excess fat and toxins 
 Supporting wound healing 
 Improving circulation and metabolism 


 Organoleptic Features 
 Punarnava acts as a mild diuretic and anti-inflammatory herb useful in edema and urinary congestion. 

 Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) 
 Gokshura is traditionally valued for supporting urinary tract function and soothing irritation. 

 Supportive Measures Mentioned Traditionally 
 The classical reference also recommends several supportive measures during treatment: 

 Yava Manda (barley water prepared from approximately 24 g barley boiled in 750 ml water and reduced to one-fourth) 
 Fresh coconut water 
 Fresh sugarcane juice 
 Bottle gourd preparations 
 Ash gourd preparations 
 Cucumber 
 Black Nightshade leaves (Solanum nigrum) 
 Punarnava leaves 
 Kasni leaves (Cichorium intybus) 

 Warm hip-bath therapy (Avagaha Sweda) is also considered beneficial for relieving pain and urinary spasm. 

 Additional Traditional Combination 
 The text also mentions administration of: 

 Hajrul Yahud Bhasma processed with radish juice (Raphanus sativus) along with the Kashayam for enhanced benefit in urinary stone disorders.
sections.precautions:
Use only under supervision of a qualified Ayurvedic physician. 
 Persistent urinary obstruction or severe pain requires medical evaluation. 
 Patients with dehydration should maintain proper fluid intake. 
 Excessively salty, spicy, and dehydrating foods should be avoided during therapy. 


 Conclusion 
 Ashmarihar Kashayam is a classical Ayurvedic decoction formulated for urinary stones, gravel, urinary obstruction, and renal pain. Prepared with herbs such as Pashanbheda (Bergenia ligulata), Varuna (Crataeva nurvala), Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa), Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris), and Guduchi (Tinospora cordifolia), the formulation works through diuretic, anti-inflammatory, and stone-breaking actions. It helps relieve urinary discomfort, supports healthy urine flow, and assists in reducing stone formation naturally. With proper dietary regulation and supervised use, Ashmarihar Kashayam remains an important Ayurvedic remedy for urinary tract disorders.

 Introduction
